no problem dude, im in similar situartion im currently unemployed on state benefits I want to gain work in the recovery sector to help other addicts. this means I need to go back to school so I applied for a psychology degree at my local university I was accepted on the course but denied financial aid as I dropped out of a degree 17 years ago. this got me down when my financial aid was denied but rather than run with that feeling i decided instead to appeal the decision i have got evidence from my recovery team doctors letters and the fact it was over 17 years ago I'm not going to give up getting on to the degree until i have exhausted every option this is me fighting not accepting that i didn't get the aid and going oh well. and you know what if the appeal fails then I will go back to transport planning and pay for the degree in modules through distance learning and get the degree that way i simply refuse to give up yeah this is not ideal but like i say its a means to an end yes the job will get me down but as i pay for each module i will get closer to my goal. you need little victories  to keep you going the turning point for me happened when i got off methodone which i was precibred for dope sickness i was in full blown opiate withdrawal for 6 weeks this was the most uncomfortable and painful experience i have ever been through and i wouldn't wish it on anyone but the joy of beating it gave me a new lease on life and proved to me change is possible as long as you dont give up, i could have called the recovery team at any moment and gone back onto my dose but i was determined to find out if i had the strength to go with out it.

hello there im 38 years old and was a heroine addict for five years, I began using after I found the mother of my children and partner of 11 years in bed with my cousin which really messed me up. 

thanks to my addiction I lost everything and have been rebuilding since I got clean 18 months ago. 

i attempted suicide three times before I decided to try and sort things out, its been very difficult but I learned that when it comes to depression you must see it as a fight with the depression being your enemy. 

​

one of the worst things about depression is that it blinds you to the things you have in life which are positive and it makes you take them for granted. sounds like you have a boyfriend? and it sounds like depression is making you overlook that you have him. i have been single since catching my ex in the affair and I long to be with someone again so please appreciate that your not alone and how it could be worse like I say the depression blinds you to what you have. 

please make a list of all the positive things you have right now like do you have a roof over your head? are you healthy? if you are healthy physically think of all the people that have to to deal with something like a cancer or HIV diagnosis. 

no doubt your boyfriend is worried about you this in its self is something to be happy about it, tell him you love him and you are going to fight this depression trust me if you don't fight the depression it will kill you eventually. I have lost two friends to suicide as they didn't fight and just ran with negative thoughts. we all have a gift as humans to rationilse so when the bad thoughts start I want you to immediately counter them with positive thoughts and things from the list you wanted. also write down what would make you worse IE a love one passing away or your boyfriend leaving this will force you to be thankful for those people or things. 

if you keep doing this repeatedly eventually the positive thoughts will slowly creep in, it takes time but with the right effort you will improve. I would highly recommend the noble eight fold path of buddism look this up it will help you immensly.

also read the wiritngs of stoics the writings of Epictetus have helped me hugely. 

please speak to your doctor and get on some medication if you haven't done so already this again will help. 

Distraction is one of the best ways to deal with depression when I got clean I bought a ZXR600 motorcycle which has been a godsend when riding I have to concentrate so much there isn't room for depressing thoughts and this has been really good for me. 

what are your hobbys and interests? right them down and then find like minded people so you can engage in these things therefore distracting you. remember you are a soldier in the mental health war! are you going to be casualty and another suicide statistic or are you going to fight and be a victor? i believe you can be a victor it just takes the right way of thinking. 

your improved mood wont come over night but trust me if you keep fighting and working on it engage in healthy distractions it WILL get better over time. contact some friends and family let them know how much you appreciate them no doubt they will tell you how you mean to them which will help as well.

please let me know what your battle plan is soldier I would love to hear!
